title: BrowserOS macOS compiled binary signature repair — Cycle 12 weak-spot closure
problem: BrowserOS server production binaries produced by `bun build --compile` were killed by macOS with SIGKILL (exit code 137) immediately on launch. `codesign --sign -` reported 'invalid or unsupported format for signature'. This blocked the server build smoke test and any portable install path that depends on a runnable compiled binary.
root_cause: Bun v1.3.12 regression on macOS arm64: compiled Mach-O binaries have a corrupt/truncated LC_CODE_SIGNATURE. The kernel's AMFI rejects the binary before `main()` runs, so `--version` and the actual server both exit 137 with no output. Verified independently with a minimal `console.log('hello')` compiled binary (also killed).
fix: Added a post-compile signature-repair step in `scripts/build/server/compile.ts` for macOS targets: strip the broken Bun-generated signature with `codesign --remove-signature` and apply a fresh ad-hoc signature with `codesign --force --sign -`. Made the step best-effort so cross-compilation environments that lack `codesign` only log a warning instead of failing the build.
tests: bun test apps/server/tests/build.test.ts PASS (2 pass, 0 fail)
open trios.app relaunched; curl http://127.0.0.1:9105/health returns ok
follow_up: Remove the signature-repair workaround once the project upgrades to Bun >= 1.3.13 (oven-sh/bun#29272).
Add a CI step that verifies the compiled binary launches on the target OS before publishing artifacts.
Consider adding an optional entitlements file for the server binary if macOS hardened runtime becomes required.
